_meta.description: Provenance registry for sense-assignment runs. Each prompt_id names a specific prompt-contract/model combination. Named acceptance policies, not numeric tiers, decide which model claims may enter a live deck. Historical capability_tier fields remain descriptive migration metadata only.

sd-cop-v1.notes: Menu-pick only — Gemini picks a sense from the SpanishDict menu; no off-menu proposal path.

sd-cop-v2.notes: Classify-or-propose — Gemini may return sense=null and propose an off-menu meaning (pos/type/construction). The gap-fill / off-menu signature in the data.

sd-cop-v3.notes: Same classify-or-propose prompt as sd-cop-v2 on the newer gemini-3.5-flash-lite. Higher tier: supersedes sd-cop-v2 answers once the tier-based resolver is wired. Current default (SD_DEFAULT_MODEL); step_6c stamps new runs with this id.

sd-lexical-v1-g31.notes: Lexical WSD only. Picks a stable menu sense or proposes a short missing lexical gloss, including genuine slang. Proper-noun, usage-tag, construction and POS decisions are owned by separate upstream evidence layers; construction-only and excluded material must abstain.

sd-lexical-v2-g35.notes: Gemini 3.5 successor to sd-lexical-v1-g31. Preserves the menu-first lexical-only contract and adds exact one-call-per-example, verbatim menu-id, and non-empty null-answer requirements after 74 invalid outputs were observed in the completed 3.1 reports.

sd-lexical-v2-g31.notes: Revised lexical-only prompt on the validated Gemini 3.1 baseline. Same semantic contract as v1 plus exact output-completeness requirements. Evaluation candidate until explicitly accepted.

sd-lexical-v2-g25.notes: Cost-control evaluation candidate using the exact revised lexical-only prompt. Never accepted merely because it is cheaper.

legacy-unknown.notes: Pre-provenance assignment. Exact model/prompt is not recoverable from the stored format (bare menu-picks look identical across 2.5 and 3.1). Any stamped run supersedes this tier.

embed-gloss-classgap-hub-v1.notes: Not a generative prompt. Sense vector from the English gloss '"word" (POS): translation — context'; sentence embedded once; nearest sense by cosine after subtracting a per-sense hubness offset measured offline against a fixed background sample; confidence is the gap between the top two MEANINGS, not leaves. Precision measured on a hand-labelled panel at Data/Spanish/Intermediates/wsd_sense_harness: 100% acceptable at gap>=0.035, 91.9% at gap>=0.021, 84.5% overall.

embed-gloss-tuplegap-hub-v1.notes: Gloss embeddings; confidence is the gap between the top two lemma+POS readings.

sd-beto-cal-v1.notes: Gloss embeddings + BETO token prototypes + clitic gate, ranked by a learned calibrator.

sd-beto-cal-v2.notes: Same stack as sd-beto-cal-v1, calibrator retrained on ok_leaf instead of ok_tup. v1's score predicted lemma+POS, 88.7% accurate on dictionary gold and nearly saturated; the exact leaf the card prints is 53.1% on the same 16,016 rows. Held-out precision of the top decile: 82.5%->99.7% under the v1 target vs 49.4%->89.1% under v2's. feature_version 5 adds five grammatical-construction features (gerund/participle/infinitive) and fixes the case where companion_of parsed 'used with a gerund' as the literal token "a", scoring the correct periphrastic leaf as construction-violating. Those features were a wash on dictionary gold (0.2% of rows carry one); kept for the lyric distribution, where the class was 15% of a 200-card hand-graded sample. Band cuts are precision targets on LEAF correctness (90% high, 70% medium) and are NOT comparable to v1's.

sd-beto-cal-v3.notes: sd-beto-cal-v2 plus the BETO tuple vote: where the token prototypes' own top-two similarity gap is >= 0.02, BETO DECIDES the (headword, POS) tuple and the gloss embedding picks the leaf inside it. Before this, BETO only contributed an advisory `token_agrees` feature to the calibrator and could never overturn a pick. Hand-graded on all 88 picks it changes: 60 better, 13 worse, 15 neutral (+2.6pp). The gate is essential -- ungated the same override graded 20/13/7, a wash, because BETO's noun bias on noun/verb homographs sits exactly where its prototypes are near-tied. Query-locality alternatives were measured on 24,675 gold rows in the same pass and rejected (window: leaf 53.09%->47.31%; mark_prefix: 52.42%).

sd-beto-cal-esc-v1.notes: Low-confidence cases sent to Gemini for a second opinion; Gemini wins on disagreement.

sd-beto-cal-esc-v2.notes: Escalation half of sd-beto-cal-v2: the low band goes to flash-lite for a closed-set second opinion. Same prompt contract as sd-beto-cal-esc-v1; the id moves with the classifier version so one card's provenance names one run, not a family.

sd-beto-cal-esc-v3.notes: Escalation half of sd-beto-cal-v3. Prompt contract unchanged from esc-v2; the id moves with the classifier version so one card's provenance names one run.

sd-beto-cal-align-v4.notes: Aligned-English leaf correction on top of sd-beto-cal-v3. mBERT SimAlign aligns the Spanish target token to its English subtitle word; where a candidate leaf's gloss head is that word, that leaf is taken. Authored ONLY on the occurrences it changes -- an untouched occurrence keeps its sd-beto-cal-v3 claim, so a card's provenance names the run that actually decided it. Measured before it was built: 49 better / 12 worse on 100 fresh hand-graded speech cards, firing on ~16%. It is the only added signal that has beaten plain gloss-cosine on this problem, because alignment matches on RELATION (which English word IS this token) where every rejected signal matched on PRESENCE (this topic is nearby) -- see docs/reference/wsd_dead_ends.md. Requires parallel text, so it is structurally a speech-mode signal; artist mode has translations for some songs only. Does not overturn sd-beto-cal-esc-v3: escalated picks graded ~88% and the alignment result was measured against the local path. Abstains where several leaves share the aligned word as a head -- the signal identified a gloss, not a leaf.

speech-beto-cal-v3-pinned.description: Speech mode on the v3 calibrated stack. Only sd-beto-cal-v3 / -esc-v3 may author sense claims, so a speech deck is attributable to one run exactly as the artist deck is. The older embed-gloss-* runs are excluded by design, not by quality -- they predate the leaf-target calibrator and the BETO tuple vote, and mixing them in makes the builder union senses across methods (which is how stale provenance reached the artist deck's cards).

speech-beto-cal-v4-pinned.description: Speech mode on the v3 calibrated stack PLUS the aligned-English leaf corrector. Three ids author claims and they do not overlap on an occurrence: sd-beto-cal-align-v4 exists only where alignment overturned the local pick, sd-beto-cal-esc-v3 only where Gemini was asked, sd-beto-cal-v3 everywhere else. Isolation is preserved in the sense that matters -- one occurrence, one authoring run -- which is not true of accepting two generations of the same classifier, where the builder unions senses and stale meanings survive.
